diagnostic_evidence.quote: first- and second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions are shown
we obtain first-order necessary optimality conditions and sufficient second-order optimality conditions

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and the opening of Section 3 say that necessary and sufficient second-order optimality conditions are proved. The paper proves only a first-order necessary condition (1st_opt_cond) and a sufficient growth-type condition (Theorem strictilocalopt, whose proof is merely sketched). A second-order necessary condition appears only as a citation to external work (the 'slightly weaker version' with the factor 1/2). The introduction itself says only 'first-order necessary ... and sufficient second-order'. The abstract and Section 3 therefore overstate what is established.

failure_location.quote: prove first- and -- necessary and sufficient -- second-order optimality conditions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract and the Section 3 introduction to say that first-order necessary and second-order sufficient conditions are proved. Alternatively, add a proof or precise citation of a second-order necessary condition for this problem.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope of the optimality-condition contribution is overstated. No formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Abstract claims necessary second-order conditions that are never proved
issues.why_classification: Rewording removes the overclaim and every proved result remains correct.

issues.failure_explanation: A measure condition |{|z^i|<=eps}| <= c_i eps^{gamma_i} yields a growth constant that decreases as c_i increases (roughly of order (c M)^{-1/gamma}). It cannot be max c_i. The same adjoint satisfies the measure condition with arbitrarily large c_i, but the growth inequality cannot then hold with that large constant. So the displayed claim with tilde c = max c_i is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the growth holds with some constant tilde c > 0 depending on the c_i, the eps_i and the L^infty bound of U_ad, for example proportional to a negative power of max c_i.
issues.overall_effect: Only the quantitative constant in this informal sufficient-condition discussion is wrong. The qualitative implication (measure condition implies L^1 growth with exponent 1+1/gamma) is the standard one.
issues.title: Growth constant in the first-variation growth claim is wrongly identified as max c_i
issues.why_classification: Local correction of the constant. The exponent, the method and the later use of Assumption (controlgrowth) are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The existence of a solution to the semidiscrete problem follows from the arguments given in the proof of
We note that $\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_h$ denotes a local solution to the semidiscrete problem.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem exist_and_conv_sol_var asserts only existence 'of a solution' of a semidiscrete problem posed over all of U_ad. J_h is never defined there. The discrete state equation is uniquely solvable only for controls near ubar, so J_h is not defined on all of U_ad. The proof is a pointer to a theorem of another paper. The proof of thm:added-2 invokes this theorem for a different problem, the minimization of J_h over U_ad ∩ B_eps(ubar), which the theorem does not cover. It then passes to the limit h->0 (weak-* convergence of minimizers to a minimizer of J) with no proof that the discrete states and costs converge for weakly-* converging controls. It also never shows that the minimizers on the closed L^1-ball are interior, hence local minimizers, before the strong-convergence step. These ingredients are either unproved or outside the cited result.

failure_location.quote: this problem admits a global solution

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define J_h on the localized set U_ad ∩ B_eps(ubar) using the unique discrete state near ybar. Prove existence of a minimizer on that set. Prove convergence of discrete states and costs under weak-* convergence of controls. Show that minimizers are interior for small h.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of the discrete optimal controls ubar_h, their local-minimizer property and the convergence ubar_h -> ubar in L^1 are not established. The error estimates use exactly these facts ('Since ubar_h -> ubar when h -> 0').
issues.title: Convergence of discrete solutions rests on an existence result for a different (localized) problem and on unproved passage to the limit
issues.why_classification: A contained set of lemmas (standard discretization-convergence arguments) closes the gap without changing the architecture or the final rates.

issues.failure_explanation: From ||y_{ubar_h} - ybar_h||_{L^2} <= C h^2, interpolation (y in H^2 only) and inverse estimates give at best ||grad(y_{ubar_h} - ybar_h)||_{L^{6/5}} <~ h^{-1} h^2 = h. This is also the order of the H^1 finite element error. The claimed O(h^2) would need W^{3,.}-type regularity, which is unavailable on a convex polytope. With O(h), (z_h-barzh) gives ||grad(zhat_h - zbar_h)||_{L^2} <~ h, not h^2. Then for n=3, (u-u-hleqz_H1) contains h^{-1/2}·h = h^{1/2}. This yields ||ubar_h - ubar||_{L^1}^{1/gamma} <~ h^{1/2}, i.e. only the rate h^{gamma/2}, not (h|log h|)^gamma.

failure_location.quote: Finally, using interpolation and inverse estimates, and estimate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the H^{-1} norm of b(e;.,zhat_h)+b(.;e,zhat_h) with e = y_{ubar_h} - ybar_h directly by ||e||_{L^2}||zhat_h||_{W^{1,3}}. Do this by moving the derivative onto zhat_h through antisymmetry or integration by parts, treating the div(w) term. This uses the existing bound (hat_z_W14) and gives h^2 without any W^{1,6/5} estimate.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof does not support the headline rate (h|log h|)^gamma for n=3, nor the matching L^2 state estimate in cor:added-1.
issues.title: Unsupported O(h^2) bound for the W^{1,6/5} norm of the discrete state error; with the supported O(h) the stated rate fails for n=3
issues.why_classification: The stated justification is false, but a short alternative estimate recovers the same rate. This needs a contained new argument, not new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper proves only ||z - zhat_h||_{L^infty} <~ h|log h| (Proposition max_norm_estimate_zz), obtained via a Stokes max-norm result and a splitting. The remark replaces it by a log-free bound h||z||_{H^2} for the Galerkin approximation of an Oseen-type adjoint, with no argument. Interpolation alone gives this order for I_h z, not for the Galerkin solution. Passing from the H^1 error O(h) to L^infty via the 2D discrete Sobolev inequality leaves a logarithmic factor. A log-free max-norm estimate under only H^2 regularity is a nontrivial claim that is neither proved nor referenced.

failure_location.quote: For the case $n=2$ we can remove the logarithmic term in the estimate of Theorem \ref{thm:estimate_control}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either supply a proof or reference for a log-free L^infty error bound of the discrete adjoint under H^2 regularity, or withdraw the remark and keep the (h|log h|)^gamma rate for n=2.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised improved n=2 rates ||ubar_h - ubar||_{L^1} <~ h^gamma and ||ybar - ybar_h||_{L^2} <~ h^gamma are unsupported. The main theorem with the logarithm is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed removal of the logarithm for n=2 relies on an unproved log-free maximum-norm estimate for the finite element approximation
issues.why_classification: Withdrawing the claim leaves a comparable (slightly weaker) result, but a stated improvement is lost, so a minor tag would understate it.
